manuscript_definition: Table 1 equation not supplied; repository reference says mu is scale and mean
code_definition: Support [0,infinity); f=exp(-t/mu)/mu; F=1-exp(-t/mu); Q=-mu*ln(1-p); mean=mu; variance=mu^2; M1(t)=mu*gammainc(2,t/mu)

manuscript_definition: Table 1 equation not supplied; repository reference says no mass before shift and total mean shift+mu
code_definition: For x=t-shift>=0: f=exp(-x/mu)/mu; F=1-exp(-x/mu); Q=shift-mu*ln(1-p); mean=shift+mu; sd=mu; M1=shift*F+mu*gammainc(2,x/mu)
comment: Code parameter is named shift; article scripts rename it t0 in outputs.

manuscript_definition: mu=physical mean and sigma=physical standard deviation
code_definition: Support (0,infinity); physical IG density with lambda=mu^3/sigma^2; mean=mu; variance=sigma^2; SciPy shape=(sigma/mu)^2, scale=mu^3/sigma^2, loc=0; CDF/quantile follow that law; exact raw partial moment is implemented analytically
comment: The requested physical convention and SciPy conversion are confirmed exactly.

manuscript_definition: t0 is an added minimum age; total mean=t0+mu and sd=sigma
code_definition: T=shift+X with X physical IG(mu,sigma); support (shift,infinity); PDF/CDF/Q all use SciPy loc=shift; mean=shift+mu; variance=sigma^2; M1_T(t)=shift*F_X(t-shift)+M1_X(t-shift)
comment: The shift is applied once and to every distributional operation.

manuscript_definition: Table 1 equation not supplied; repository reference says gamma shape k and scale theta
code_definition: Support [0,infinity); f=t^(k-1) exp(-t/scale)/(Gamma(k) scale^k); F=P(k,t/scale); SciPy quantile; mean=k*scale; variance=k*scale^2; M1=k*scale*P(k+1,t/scale)

manuscript_definition: Table 1 equation not supplied; repository reference says uniform from tmin to tmin+delta
code_definition: Support [tmin,tmin+delta]; f=1/delta; clipped linear CDF; Q=tmin+p*delta; mean=tmin+delta/2; variance=delta^2/12; M1=(u^2-tmin^2)/(2 delta), u=clip(t,tmin,tmin+delta)
comment: delta is a width, not the upper endpoint.

code_definition: Atoms are at mu1 and mu1+mu2 with masses rate and 1-rate; CDF is the weighted sum of indicators; Q chooses the first atom for p<=rate; mean=mu1+(1-rate)mu2; sd=sqrt(rate(1-rate))*abs(mu2)
comment: The two physical positions requested are exactly mu1 and mu1+mu2. pdf() is a display regularization, not the mathematical delta density.

manuscript_definition: Table 1 equation not supplied; repository reference says one free and one fixed atom
code_definition: Atoms at mufree and programmatic muset, masses rate and 1-rate; CDF weighted indicators; mean=rate*mufree+(1-rate)*muset; sd=sqrt(rate(1-rate))*abs(muset-mufree); no partial moment is used
comment: The generalized quantile assumes the free atom is first; distributed bounds cap mufree at the default muset=70, so the canonical configuration respects that ordering.

manuscript_definition: Dirac at mu1; exponential starts at mu1+t0; mu2 is its scale; r is Dirac mass
code_definition: Full law: rate*delta_mu1 +(1-rate)*Exp(loc=mu1+shift,scale=mu2); support is {mu1} union [mu1+shift,infinity); full CDF and generalized Q are implemented; mean=rate*mu1+(1-rate)(mu1+shift+mu2); continuous partial moment is normalized before the engine applies 1-rate once
function: get_dirac_time; continuous_support_start; cdf; cdf_inv; mean; std; continuous_cdf_and_partial_first_moment
comment: Normalization is correct. pdf() returns only the weighted ordinary continuous density because a Dirac has no ordinary-function density.

code_definition: Default bounded edges [0,20,40,60,200] yr. vj=logistic(zj); fj=remaining*vj sequentially and final fraction=remaining, followed by normalization. PDF is fj/bin_width on [left,right), with the final [left,right] closed. CDF/Q, mean=sum(fj*midpoint), variance including within-bin variance, and exact piecewise partial moment are implemented
function: bin_edges; fractions; pdf; cdf; cdf_inv; mean; std; cdf_and_partial_first_moment
comment: The generic old bin is finite by default; support_open also ends at a finite configured support_end_max. Holten's >60 endmember is a separate case-specific construction.
